ai.description: *Ovophis zayuensis* reaches 60–80 cm. It is brown with dark, irregular dorsal blotches and a distinct triangular head. It features a prominent dark postocular stripe and keeled scales.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Ovophis zayuensis* is best distinguished by its distinct, dark-edged, reddish-brown dorsal blotches that are separated by narrow, pale interspaces, unlike the more uniform patterns of other Indian pit vipers.
ai.habitat: *Ovophis zayuensis* inhabits dense, humid subtropical broadleaf forests and temperate mixed woodlands at elevations typically ranging from 1,500 to 2,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Zayuan Mountain Pit Viper is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter and rocks to ambush passing prey under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Ovophis zayuensis* is oviparous, laying clutches of 6–10 eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, with hatchlings typically appearing in late summer or autumn.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Ovophis zayuensis* is found in the eastern Himalayas of Arunachal Pradesh, India, typically inhabiting high-altitude forests between 1,500 and 2,500 meters.
